speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if your double vision or weakness fluctuates throughout the day, perhaps getting worse as the day progresses? I also need to know if you have any difficulty swallowing or speaking.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Does the weakness or double vision improve after a short rest, and do you have any difficulty swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty swallowing or changes in your speech? I would also like to check your eye movements; please follow my finger with your eyes only as I move it up, down, left, and right.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: I would like to examine your eyes closely for ptosis, so please keep your eyes open and look straight ahead. I will also perform a physical exam to check for proximal muscle weakness by having you rise from a chair without using your arms.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss.
